nom: Murad City Skin Age Defense Broad Spectrum SPF 50 / PA++++

segments.oily: Some oily-skin reviewers report the product does not increase shine or breakouts and works well as a base, while a sensitive-dry reviewer with rosacea explicitly warns oily-skin users may find it too greasy.
segments.dry: Reviewers with dry skin describe it as moisturizing and dewy, non-drying, and a good daily choice, though one dry-skin reviewer found it dried her skin out and looked bad under makeup.
segments.combination: Combination-skin reviewers note it goes on smoothly with no white cast, but one reports getting noticeably oilier in her oily zones after application.
segments.sensitive: Sensitive-skin reviewers are split: many with sensitive, acne-prone, rosacea, or eczema-prone skin say it is the only sunscreen that doesn't irritate or break them out, while others with sensitive skin report itching, rash, burning, or redness.
segments.mature: One reviewer in her 30s with sensitive, dry, rosacea-prone mature skin calls it dermatologist-approved and a holy grail despite slight greasiness.

concerns.aging: One reviewer citing improved skin pigmentation and general anti-aging protection is satisfied; no dissent reported specifically on aging.
concerns.dehydration: Multiple dry-skin reviewers describe it as hydrating, moisturizing and dewy with no dryness; however, at least two reviewers report it dried out their skin or was overly drying and peeled with moisturizers underneath.
concerns.redness: Rosacea and redness-prone reviewers mostly report no flares and calming wear, but one sensitive-skin reviewer had persistent redness and burning after application.
concerns.barrier: Reviewers with compromised or reactive barriers (eczema, rosacea) report no irritation and comfortable daily wear; conversely, several sensitive-skin reviewers experienced itching, splotchiness, or burning suggesting barrier reactivity.
concerns.spots: One reviewer with melasma reports the product finally gave her adequate lightweight daily protection; no dissent noted on pigmentation-related spots.
concerns.blemishes: Many acne-prone reviewers report it does not clog pores or cause breakouts and is safe for acne-prone skin; no reviewer explicitly reports new breakouts from this product.
concerns.oiliness: Oily-skin and combination reviewers mostly report a non-greasy, matte-ish finish with no added oiliness, but one combination-skin reviewer and one dry/sensitive-rosacea reviewer note it can feel greasy or increase oil in oily areas.

extraits.titre: Did Not Work for Sensitive Skin
extraits.texte: Disclaimer: I have EXTREMELY sensitive skin to SPF, so I'm not sure if I should give this such a low rating, because it's probably just me, not the product. I have yet to find an SPF that does not cause my skin to start itching and to develop a rash, and this was no exception. If I had normal skin, I would've liked this SPF - it didn't smell bad, it went on smoothly, it was easy to dispense....but it unfortunately made my skin very itchy and splotchy.

I really wanted to like this, but as soon as I applied it my skin started burning. My skin was also red even after I removed it. I made the switch to mineral spf bc some chemical spf's gave me the same reaction. I wasn't expecting a mineral sunscreen to do the same. I think I would like this product if my skin wasn't super sensitive. It was lightweight and had no white cast. If you have sensitive skin though I would definitely be cautious about this one.

This is such a nice light sunscreen. Didn't clog my pores, went seamlessly under makeup, and didn't leave a white cast. My one complaint is that I definitely got oily a lot faster than without. I have combination skin and my oily areas are VERY oily. So if you have normal or dry skin you probably wouldn't experience that. Definitely worth a try.

I live in Southern California so I know it's especially important for me to wear spf due to the constant sun exposure but I never was able to find a sunscreen that didn't irritate my skin and make me break out all over. I saw this and was like wow that's expensive. But the ingredients are great and I took a chance on it and let me say it's phenomenal. It's thinner than a lotion but thicker than a liquid , and is very hydrating which is great for my dry sensitive skin. I can layer it over my skincare with no pilling and I can layer my makeup on top and it looks great as a base. If you have tried many sunscreens and have had no luck I strongly suggest you give this one a chance. In my opinion it's worth every penny.

I've been using this sunscreen for 2 years now. It is pricey-but it's the only one that works for my skin. Lasts me about 6 months depending on how often I need to use it (Im a home body). I have oily, acne-prone sensitive skin and hate the feeling of sunscreen on my face/the white cast some leave. this feels light, I usually use it in place of a moisturizer. It doesn't make me look like a greasy mess, but still allows me to have a healthy appearance without mattifying all my glow. Ingredients are a plus, as I can only use mineral based sunscreens (for the oceans, and my sensitive skin). The only downside is it doesn't wear the best under liquid foundation (still workable though just minor separation/creasing after a few hours) but I don't wear foundation that often anyway. Best sunscreen! (a cheap fav that reminds me of this is the Maelove one, it's a bit more matte and sort of tacky though!)

extraits.titre: Pry from my cold dead hands
extraits.texte: I have fair, sensitive, dry skin with rosacea and I'm in my 30s. My dermatologist "approved" this product because it's all physical blocking so it's perfect for my skin type. I love this stuff. When you're applying the 1/4 tsp recommended amount for ALL sunscreens, I do find that this one tends to be a little greasier than others. If you have oily skin, I don't think you would care for this product. Normal to very dry- it's gonna be your HG. I use it as a primer under my makeup and when I'm going bare-faced. Probably my favorite part about this stuff is the viscosity- it's very liquidy- more than a typical lotion, which I find terrific for coverage and lack of "skip spots." Oh- and My husband uses this sunscreen, too! Both of us each have a bottle and we go through it every couple of months. Cons: -Not ideal for POC -Not ideal for oily skin -Can get two reapplications of this, but a third is just too greasy

I like the tint on this product because it does not feel like foundation. Although, I do not think this will work well with darker skin tones. It does not leave a cast. It has a nice sheen to it despite feeling dry. Biggest problem is that it's easy to sweat it off- thus leaving you vulnerable. Additionally, it makes moisturizers peel off (or it peels off itself) when being applied. It is very lightweight. For the price I would expect that this formula would work well with different moisturizers- especially as it is VERY drying. I would recommend only for individuals who could use a bit of dryness.
